mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 5.25% over the prior 8 weeks reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in any 4-week window
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 4-week pre-trigger period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment claims exceeding 250,000 in a month coincides with a sharp decline in S&P 500 20-day forward returns as investor sentiment deteriorates on labor market weakness.
failure_condition: During periods meeting the trigger, 20-day forward returns are not statistically more negative than the 5-day pre-trigger average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds 3% in the prior month, it triggers a risk premium increase on equities, pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not more negative than the 1-day pre-inflation surprise average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105 suggests accelerating supply growth, which typically coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates further economic expansion.
failure_condition: Over 10 consecutive months with INDPRO > 105, 20-day forward returns show no outperformance versus the pre-expansion average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in the unemployment rate below 3.5% indicate a tightening labor market, which, when coupled with rising FEDFUNDS, amplifies the discount rate effect and produces negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5 and FEDFUNDS increases over the same period
regime_hint: labor market tightening coupled with rate hikes
failure_condition: During the identified trigger regime, 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 60-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) by over 100,000 indicates weakening labor demand, which is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate slower growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by more than 100000 in a single month
failure_condition: During such PAYEMS drops, 20-day forward returns are not more negative than the 5-day pre-drop average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly retail sales (not in observable list, so skip) — instead, use HOUST as proxy for demand — unexpectedly decline for two consecutive months, it signals softening demand, leading to negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns during the two-month decline are not more negative than the prior month's average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 4-week decline in the monthly index of industrial production (INDPRO) below 105 suggests supply constraints, which often precede a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates price adjustments.
failure_condition: Over 8 consecutive weeks with INDPRO < 105, 20-day forward returns show no outperformance versus the pre-constraint average (p > 0.05).
